title: Move Atlas database from MongoDB to PostgreSQL
summary: Atlas will standardise on PostgreSQL after repeated consistency and query-cost problems with MongoDB.
reason: MongoDB could not provide transactional consistency across the reporting aggregates, joins between customer and usage data required expensive application-side stitching, and our managed MongoDB costs grew 3.4x year over year. PostgreSQL gives us ACID transactions, relational joins, mature tooling and a single operational model with the rest of NovaTech.

alternatives.name: Stay on MongoDB
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: continued data-stitching cost and no transactional reporting.

alternatives.name: Adopt a hosted analytics warehouse
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: overkill for operational workloads, new skills required.

alternatives.name: PostgreSQL on AWS RDS
alternatives.outcome: Selected: relational integrity, existing team expertise, lower cost.

title: Use FalkorDB as the graph store for Nova
summary: Nova's company knowledge graph will live in FalkorDB, queried with Cypher for relationship-aware retrieval.
reason: Company questions are relationship questions: who owns what, what supports which decision. Vector similarity alone cannot answer multi-hop queries. FalkorDB gives us Redis-compatible low-latency Cypher traversal over people, projects, documents and decisions.

alternatives.name: Vector-only RAG
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: cannot answer ownership or decision-trace questions.

alternatives.name: Neo4j
alternatives.outcome: Considered: heavier operational footprint for a hackathon-scale deployment.

alternatives.name: FalkorDB
alternatives.outcome: Selected: fast Cypher traversal, Redis protocol, simple deployment.

title: Standardise new web apps on React with Vite and TypeScript
summary: All new internal and customer web frontends use React, Vite and TypeScript.
reason: Vite cut our median dev-server start from 41s to under 1s, TypeScript catches contract drift against the FastAPI layer at compile time, and React keeps hiring and onboarding simple.

alternatives.name: Continue with Create React App
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: unmaintained tooling, slow builds.

alternatives.name: Vue
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: team already productive in React.

title: Run production workloads on AWS EKS
summary: All production services move to Kubernetes on AWS EKS with GitOps deployments.
reason: We were running a patchwork of EC2 and Lambda deployments with no uniform rollout story. EKS gives one deployment model, node autoscaling and a single place to enforce policy.

alternatives.name: Remain on EC2 + systemd
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: no standard rollout or scaling story.

alternatives.name: AWS ECS
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: team already has Kubernetes skills from prior roles.

title: Python and FastAPI as the standard backend stack
summary: New backend services are written in Python 3.12 with FastAPI.
reason: FastAPI gives typed request/response models, automatic OpenAPI docs and async I/O with a small footprint. Python is already the language of the data and ML teams, which removes translation layers between data pipelines and services.

alternatives.name: Node.js/Express
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: weaker fit with data tooling.

alternatives.name: Go
alternatives.outcome: Deferred: performance benefits not yet required.

title: Orchestrate Nova agents with LangGraph
summary: Nova's pipeline uses LangGraph to run intent, graph, retrieval, reasoning and action agents.
reason: We need inspectable state between steps, deterministic branching on intent, and a place to attach human confirmation before actions. LangGraph's state graph maps directly onto that flow.

alternatives.name: Single prompt chain
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: no branching or confirmation points.

alternatives.name: Custom orchestration
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: reinventing checkpointing and state.

title: Use Redis for caching, sessions and job queues
summary: Redis is the company standard for ephemeral state.
reason: One operational model for cache, session store and background job queue removed three bespoke components.

alternatives.name: Separate Memcached + RabbitMQ
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: more moving parts for marginal gain.

title: Adopt OIDC with a dedicated Auth Gateway in Orion
summary: All products authenticate through an Orion-managed OIDC gateway instead of per-service sessions.
reason: Session logic was duplicated across three services with divergent logout behaviour. A single gateway centralises MFA, RBAC and audit logging.

alternatives.name: Continue per-service sessions
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: divergent security behaviour.

alternatives.name: Third-party IdP only
alternatives.outcome: Under evaluation: retained as a future option.

title: Replace legacy CI with GitHub Actions
summary: All repositories move to GitHub Actions with required checks on main.
reason: Pipelines live next to the code, matrix builds are cheap, and required checks give us branch protection without a separate CI server.

alternatives.name: Self-hosted Jenkins
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: maintenance burden.

title: Add read replicas for Atlas reporting workloads
summary: Reporting queries move to a PostgreSQL read replica to protect transactional latency.
reason: After the PostgreSQL migration, dashboard queries contended with transactional writes. A replica isolates reporting with a one-minute tolerated staleness.

alternatives.name: Materialised views on primary
alternatives.outcome: Rejected: still contends for I/O.

alternatives.name: Read replica
alternatives.outcome: Selected: simple, operationally proven.
